neighbours.label: transport of energy or matter along a path from a source to a destination ('on the way from the plant to your home', 'leaves the body unchanged')
fire: A lot of electricity is wasted on the way from the original generating station to the houses it serves.
Much of the oil is spilled on its way from the original well to the refinery.
The vitamin is not absorbed and passes out of the body unchanged.
Heat escapes through the walls on the way from the boiler to the radiators upstairs.
Gas is piped from the field to the coast before it reaches the export terminal.
Some of the signal is lost along the cable from the antenna to the receiver.
Why haul coal across the country instead of bringing it from the mine next door?
Water loses pressure on its way from the original source in the hills to the city taps.
quiet: The generating station is old and is run by a small team of engineers.
The oil well was drilled in 1952 and is still owned by the same family.
The vitamin is sold as small orange capsules in most chemists.
The boiler is in the basement and was serviced last spring.
The gas field was discovered by a survey ship in the late sixties.
The antenna on the roof is painted grey to match the tiles.
Coal mining was the main industry in the valley for a century.
The hills above the city are covered with pine forest and small farms.

notes: Probe: 'on the way from the original power plant to your home' 0.93 (peak ' to'), 'leaves the body unchanged' 0.52, 'from the reservoir to the town before it reaches' 0.42, 'instead of bringing it from' 0.30, farm-to-cup 0.15; static same-topic sentences 0.03-0.04. Leaks: 'transformed from one form into another' 0.22, 'does not stop with the sale' 0.27, so the near misses avoid from/to paths entirely. The - pole looks like the conversion side (card).
